title: POC scoping: benchmark harness integration - Redwood / Acme Health
summary: Redwood AE and SE aligned with Acme Health on POC success criteria, harness integration approach, workload sizing, streaming vs non-streaming test plans, and timelines. Action items include sharing harness repo, customer provisioning of test scripts and data, and scheduling load test window the week of 3/16.
action_items: Priya Nair (Redwood SE): Share benchmark harness repo, runbook, and sample config by 2026-03-12
Jenna Ortiz (Acme ML): Provide canonical inference scripts and 2 weeks of anonymized request traces by 2026-03-14
Omar Khan (Acme SRE): Open a temporary VPC peering and provide bastion host and test credentials by 2026-03-15
Alex Rivera (Redwood AE): Send draft POC success criteria doc and pricing/commit options by 2026-03-11
All: Confirm 4-hour load test window during week of 2026-03-16 by 2026-03-12
next_steps: Customer to push scripts and traces to shared S3 link
Schedule 4-hour load test and reserve Dedicated capacity if needed
Follow-up call to review initial harness runs and metrics (tentative 2026-03-18)
transcript:
[00:00] Alex (AE): okay hey everyone thanks for joining, um this is Alex from Redwood Infrence, and with me is Priya our solutions engineer. um quick round of intros?
[00:12] Mark (CTO): Mark here, CTO at Acme Health. Jenna is ML eng, Omar SRE, Lina product.
[00:18] Priya (SE): hi all, quick agenda: align on success criteria, discuss harness integration and your scripts, decide streaming vs non-streaming approach for tests, and pick timelines.
[00:30] Jenna (ML): sounds good. our main goal is to validate latency at p95 under expected load, and cost per token — we want to compare hosted vs dedicated for economics.
[00:42] Omar (SRE): plus we need to validate our VPC setup and ensure audit logs and KMS keys work during the POC.
[00:50] Alex (AE): perfect. can we capture target numbers now? what are you expecting for rps and latency?
[00:58] Jenna (ML): our production profile is roughly 40 rps average with spikes to 120 for 5-10 minutes, typical prompt lengths avg 120 tokens, max 512. target p95 latency under 350ms for streaming responses, and for non-streaming generation ideally under 600ms.
[01:20] Priya (SE): okay that helps. couple notes — streaming measurements are tricky because they depend on payload and chunking. our harness supports both streaming and non-streaming modes. we usually do prefix-caching runs as well, since many requests share prefixes.
[01:38] Mark (CTO): what do you mean by prefix caching? will that change the RPS you're able to show?
[01:44] Priya (SE): prefix/KV cache means if you have repeated prompts or conversation context, the runtime avoids recomputing earlier tokens. it can drastically reduce average latency and gpu utilization. we can run with cache off and on. we should test both to reflect worst-case and typical-case.
[01:58] Jenna (ML): on the harness side we have in-house scripts — python-based clients that call an internal endpoint. we can port them or run them through your harness. do you prefer we hand over scripts or just traces?
[02:10] Priya (SE): either works. preferred flow: you give us canonical inference scripts and a sample of request traces (timestamps + prompt + desired mode streaming vs non). we can repo-ize it quickly. we also have a sample wrapper to adapt scripts; if you prefer to run locally we can provide a runner that hits your endpoint or ours.
[02:28] Jenna (ML): ok we'll prepare the scripts. they currently do streaming chunk handling locally.
[02:34] Omar (SRE): security question: we can't send PHI, so traces will be anonymized. what's needed in traces?
[02:40] Priya (SE): we only need timing and token length distributions and a small sample of prompts with placeholders, and flags for streaming vs non-streaming. anonymized traces are fine. also we need a service account and temporary keys for the run if you want Redwood to execute the load from our side.
[02:55] Mark (CTO): about infrastructure — if we do Dedicated capacity, how much should we reserve for the 4 hour load test?
[03:02] Alex (AE): based on the numbers provided, I think a 4-GPU pool (A100-ish) should be enough to hit 120 spike rps with caching disabled for the worst-case; but Priya will validate with the harness. if you want to avoid capacity bookings we can run on Hosted but the reported latency can vary depending on noisy neighbors; Dedicated gives repeatable numbers.
[03:23] Priya (SE): yes we'll run a quick local sim with your script to estimate throughput and then recommend either Dedicated sizing or a hosted run with reserved concurrency. we'll share an estimated cost and expected p95 numbers.
[03:35] Lina (Product): what about streaming vs non-streaming — from product side we care about UX for partial tokens; we prefer streaming but want to see cost delta.
[03:44] Priya (SE): harness will measure both. streaming runs measure time-to-first-byte and full-stream completion; non-streaming measures end-to-end generation. you'll get p50/p95/p99 and token counts.
[03:55] Jenna (ML): for the harness, do you instrument for SDK vs raw HTTP? our clients use both.
[04:01] Priya (SE): yes, we have runners for REST, websocket streaming, and SDK wrappers. please tell us which SDK version and we can match it.
[04:08] Mark (CTO): security & compliance — we need SOC2/ISO references, audit logs during POC, and KMS integration proof.
[04:16] Alex (AE): we'll share our security pack and SOC2 report. for KMS we can integrate customer-managed keys in Private or Dedicated — for Hosted there are also KMS integrations but it depends on plan. we'll attach relevant docs.
[04:30] Omar (SRE): we need network diagram for peering.
[04:33] Priya (SE): we'll attach a sample diagram and steps for a temporary peering; our runbook lists the ports and bastion details.
[04:42] Jenna (ML): timeline — we'd like to run the load test in the week of 3/16 and have results by 3/19 to inform a vendor decision.
[04:49] Alex (AE): that seems doable. immediate next: Priya will push bootstrapping harness repo and runbook tomorrow; Jenna will provide scripts and traces by 3/14; Omar will provision network by 3/15; then we schedule a 4-hour window in 3/16-3/20.
[05:05] Priya (SE): on the harness side, steps: 1) clone repo, 2) update config with target endpoints, keys, mode (stream/non-stream), 3) run smoke-run at low rps, 4) run incremental ramp to target, capturing time-to-first-byte, per-chunk latencies, p95 metrics, gpu util, and token counts. we also capture logs for error rates.
[05:25] Jenna (ML): what about measuring cost — do you estimate per-token cost during the run?
[05:29] Priya (SE): yes harness records total tokens and we can apply Redwood pricing models to estimate per-token cost for hosted and an approximate cost model for Dedicated (including GPU amortization). we'll provide a spreadsheet with cost computation.
[05:41] Mark (CTO): are there gotchas when comparing streaming vs non-streaming?
[05:44] Priya (SE): streaming latency can look better for time-to-first-byte but total compute/tokens might be similar. chunking and network behavior affect apparent p95. also if you do many short responses streaming wins; for longer outputs overhead differs. we'll emphasize measuring both user-perceived latency and server compute.
[06:00] Alex (AE): ok let's talk success criteria concretely — Jenna?
[06:04] Jenna (ML): must-have: p95 latency under 350ms streaming at 40rps sustained, tolerate spikes to 120rps with p95 under 800ms; error rate under 0.5%. nice-to-have: cost per 1M tokens below our internal threshold, and consistent results + audit logs.
[06:23] Priya (SE): we'll map test scenarios: baseline (cache off, non-streaming), typical (cache on, streaming), spike test (ramp to 120 rps), and long-tail test (many long prompts).
[06:35] Omar (SRE): we'll need logs for tracing and correlation ids — can the harness inject a trace id per request?
[06:40] Priya (SE): yes the runner supports a header with request id and we record it across metrics.
[06:45] Alex (AE): any blockers?
[06:47] Mark (CTO): only internal procurement sign-off if Dedicated capacity needed, but we can use Hosted for first pass. Sam from procurement is on the call and will follow up.
[06:56] Sam (procurement): noted. we'll evaluate cost after initial results.
[06:58] Priya (SE): final note on harness: we can run tests from Redwood infra hitting your VPC, or run a customer-hosted runner that executes inside your network — both supported. if you want isolated results with KMS, we'd recommend customer-hosted runner in your VPC.
[07:18] Jenna (ML): ok we prefer customer-run inside our VPC for security. will need the runner docs.
[07:23] Priya (SE): will send runner container + helm chart and a walkthrough.
[07:28] Alex (AE): recap of action items and timeline then we'll close.
[07:35] Mark (CTO): thanks everyone, see you on the follow-up.
[07:39] [meeting ends]

Notes: occasional small transcription errors (Redwood Infrence spelled once). references: Harness repo link (shared in chat) - https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmark-harness (placeholder), POC success criteria doc (to be shared), security pack (link to S3 shared doc).
